notes: scan061.N1. This continuation contrasts arbitrary singularities in general neighbourhood pieces with the interest of starred pieces. The author explicitly gives the example of Xi=Xi* reduced to a point and says that arbitrary singularity types can appear fibrewise. The isolated page supplies the assertion and example, not a construction proving every arbitrary-type claim.

scan061.N2. Targeted check: if a starred piece is indeed a germ of an open subset of a nonsingular stratum Xk*, it remains nonsingular. Nonsingularity is local: every point of the open representative retains a nonsingular neighbourhood from the stratum. This verifies the stated local implication, conditional on the identification of the starred piece with that open germ.

scan061.N3. The fibration over Xi* with fibre denoted by the final starred neighbourhood is asserted here as the way the preceding nonsingularity will be expressed. This leaf does not establish the fibration construction or its regularity/local-triviality hypotheses. Those stronger claims are carried as background, not independently proved in this reading.

scan061.N4. The equality after pierres literally has exponent j on its left member and a star on the right. Both glyphs are clear. Scan060 (13) instead identifies the starred extreme with exponent i, subject to the qualification recorded there. The j on this leaf is preserved as a possible authorial slip; it is not changed to the expected i. The former isolated-reader suggestion of k was not used.

scan061.N5. The second paragraph states a work plan: maximize expressions using Xi* and elementary adjacent-index neighbourhoods first; then permit general i≤j; only afterward examine the broader Vi,k^j notation, with the normal-crossing-divisor case mentioned. It is not a completed proof.

scan061.N6. Revision sweep found exactly one cancelled phrase, the uncertain ce sont, and three live insertions: germe d', les, and les Xi* et. The leader of inserted les does not strike the following V; the inserted les Xi* et is attached after aussi. Dernier is live, with letter retracing and no independent cancellation.

scan061.N7. The dark upper-right 18 and pale lower-left 60 are distinct physical elements and hands. The oval around 18 is clipped/open at the top source boundary. Its surviving lower curve is encoded without supplying a top arc. No independent diagram or other drawing occurs on this leaf.

scan061.N8. Remaining local doubts are confined to the cancelled ce sont, s'exprimera/s'exprime ending, fibre z/Z, the large comma versus extra j in the second lower unstarred subscript, sans/dans, en/eu, and reduced à/colon. A complete formula is retained in every formula audit box. The preferred à after diviseurs is supported by two same-page reduced-à comparisons, but the blind reading leaves colon as an explicit alternative.

scan061.N9. H's opening note about an argument on neighbouring pages and its final enddocument are editorial material, absent from the manuscript image. They are excluded from the page without being counted as source-text corrections. The claim in that note has not been evaluated from other pages.

scan061.N10. All ten neighbourhood capitals have locally visible rounded/scripted bodies; C's plain V is changed separately at each physical occurrence. This is not a blanket alphabet replacement based only on the shared notation table. Subscript commas are likewise recorded locally rather than normalized.

scan061.N11. All seventeen differing blind boxes were adjudicated from their crops. The audit adds dans as an alternative to sans and colon as an alternative to reduced à. It retains the literal superscript j and clear right-hand star in the upper equality, the separately written un before fibré, the live first lower V and dernier, and the explicit lower index ambiguity. The repeated contracted k forms were compared with the clear angular k in the same equality; no h/u index convention is introduced. The word pierres matches the paired-r forms on scan058. Neither the uncertain cancelled phrase nor the verb suffix is resolved by grammar.
